content.title: Fonts: bundled Liberation stack, opt-in discovery
content.lede: Every conversion can use bundled Liberation Sans/Serif/Mono plus DejaVu Sans, with no font scanning unless you ask. Named CSS families resolve through pdf.FontResolver; legacy display names are not rewritten to Liberation unless you opt into metric aliases or supply the face.

items.title: Bundled faces
items.body: Default conversions embed Liberation Sans, Serif, and Mono (Regular / Bold / Italic / BoldItalic) plus DejaVu Sans for Unicode fallback and `system-ui`. Latin-1 uses a simple TrueType subset; nothing is scanned and no directories are touched.

items.title: Opt-in: discovered faces
items.body: `--font-path DIR` scans `DIR` (and children to depth 2) for `.ttf` / `.otf` and is repeatable. `--use-system-fonts` also scans common OS font directories such as `/usr/share/fonts` while skipping proprietary Windows and corefont trees. Discovery does not import Fontconfig alias rules.

items.title: Matching and fallback
items.body: `pdf.FontResolver` tries an exact registry / `@font-face` / `--font-path` match per CSS token, then continues the author stack, then expands only the generics `serif` / `sans-serif` / `monospace` / `system-ui`. Names such as Georgia or Arial are not rewritten to Liberation by default.

items.title: CJK readiness
items.body: Han, kana, and Hangul render when a capable TTF is on the font path, for example `fonts-noto-cjk`. The tiny OFL subset `NotoSansKR-HangulSubset.ttf` in `testdata/fonts` exists for CI and the fixture-27 smoke test only, not as a production CJK face.

content.heading: Font flags and discovery behavior
rows: Scan `DIR` (and children to depth 2) for `.ttf` / `.otf`; repeatable. A bare `.ttf`/`.otf` file path loads that one face.
Also scan common OS font directories (e.g. `/usr/share/fonts`); skips proprietary Windows/corefont trees. Independent of Fontconfig aliases.
After an exact registry miss, try curated accepts (Georgia→Gelasio, Courier New→Cousine, …) against already-registered faces only. Default off; the flag alone does not scan disk.
Exact name-table match first; generics expand to Liberation/DejaVu; legacy display names need a real face, `@font-face`, or the metric-alias opt-in
Missing IPA / uncommon Unicode glyphs fall back through the family stack and Liberation, then DejaVu, then any covering face on the opt-in registry
Bundled Liberation + DejaVu only; Latin-1 uses a simple TrueType subset with WinAnsi-style single-byte codes

content.heading: CJK / Hangul with --font-path
content.code:
gowkhtmltopdf --font-path /usr/share/fonts/truetype/droid \
  --font-path testdata/fonts \
  fixture-27-cjk-fontpath.html out.pdf
# Production Hangul: fonts-noto-cjk or any Hangul-capable TTF on --font-path
#   --font-path /usr/share/fonts/opentype/noto
# testdata/fonts/NotoSansKR-HangulSubset.ttf is a tiny OFL subset for CI
# and the fixture-27 smoke test only, not a full CJK face.

sections.heading: Type0 / CID for code points above U+00FF
sections.body: When a text run contains code points above U+00FF (after punctuation folding), the writer switches that run onto a Type0 / CIDFontType2 sibling resource with Identity-H encoding and Unicode CIDs. Glyphs must exist in the selected face; Liberation Sans alone still shows `?` for CJK.

sections.heading: Arabic and Hebrew: OT shaping via go-text/typesetting
sections.body: OpenType shaping runs through the allowlisted pure-Go module `github.com/go-text/typesetting` (`CGO_ENABLED=0`) when the active face has a GSUB table. `TextShow` / `ShapeTextFont` drive the pure-Go HarfBuzz port, then reverse-cmap shaped glyphs to Unicode CIDs for Type0 Identity-H.
bullets: OT joining and ligation (e.g. Lam-Alef) apply when GSUB is present and the reverse-cmap covers the glyphs.
Fallback with no face, no GSUB, or unmapped glyphs: RTL run reverse plus best-effort presentation-form joining in `ShapeText`.
Faces with neither Presentation Forms nor a usable GSUB reverse-cmap will still look disconnected.
Real CGO HarfBuzz is rejected; `TestDirectModuleAllowlist` pins the module list.

sections.heading: CJK needs a capable face
sections.body: CJK (Han, kana, Hangul) works when a capable TTF is on the font path; Hangul specifically needs `fonts-noto-cjk` or any Hangul-capable TTF on `--font-path`. `writing-mode: vertical-rl|lr` is parsed but lays out as a horizontal block. In mixed Latin + CJK runs, Latin glyphs missing from the CJK face are drawn with embedded Liberation while CJK continues on the Type0 sibling of the original face.

sections.heading: Indic and other complex scripts: partial
sections.body: OpenType applies when the face and reverse-cmap succeed, but production Indic quality is not claimed beyond that. The fallback keeps combining marks after the base with no in-tree matra reordering.

sections.heading: @font-face: local and https TTF/OTF/WOFF1/WOFF2
sections.body: `convert.MergeFontFaces` registers document faces on both PDF and image paths. Supported `src` values are fetched via `FetchSub` under the same ACL, network policy, timeout, and body cap as CSS and images.
bullets: Local `url(...ttf|otf|woff|woff2)` under `--allow-local-files` / `--allow`, and `https://` / `http://` of those formats, decompress then `ParseTTF` (TrueType outlines only).
WOFF2 uses allowlisted `tdewolff/font.ParseWOFF2` (`DecodeWOFF2`), then the same TrueType path as WOFF1/TTF.
`.eot` and `data:` sources are skipped with a warning. CFF/`OTTO` and variable fonts (`fvar`) are rejected.
`font-weight` and `font-style` on `@font-face` are retained and applied as Registry style overrides; omitted descriptors keep the face file's macStyle bits.

content.title: Rejected and skipped formats
content.body: CFF / `OTTO` OpenType and variable fonts (`fvar`) are rejected: TrueType outlines only, static faces. `.eot` and `data:` `@font-face` sources are skipped with a warning. HTTP `Content-Encoding: br` on ordinary fetches is still absent; that is separate from WOFF2's on-disk Brotli payload, which `DecodeWOFF2` already handles.
